#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=gromacstest
#   --partition=GPU
#   --gres=gpu:1
#   --ntasks=10
#   --cpus-per-task=1
#   --time=01:00:00

#flux: --job-name=gromacstest
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 10
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=1h

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: --partition=GPU
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run on non-GPU nodes or have different limits/priority (or be rejected by policy).

export GMX_IMGDIR=${SIFDIR}/gromacs/
export GMX_IMG=gromacs-2022.3_20230206.sif
export TOPOL_FILE=topol.tpr

# SLURM_NTASKS is not set under Flux; use the requested task count (10).
# Run a single Gromacs instance using 10 OpenMP threads.
singularity run --nv -B "${PWD}:/host_pwd" --pwd /host_pwd "$GMX_IMGDIR/$GMX_IMG" \
  gmx mdrun -ntmpi 1 -nb gpu -pin on -v -noconfout -nsteps 5000 -ntomp 10 -s "$TOPOL_FILE"

reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job specified a GPU partition (`--partition=GPU`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition selection; on sites where this affects eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.

The resource section requests 10 tasks (`#flux: -n 10`), but the workload is a single Gromacs instance using 10 OpenMP threads (`-ntmpi 1 ... -ntomp 10`). This indicates a mismatch: it should request 1 task with 10 cores rather than 10 tasks.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash

#SBATCH --job-name=gromacstest
#This sets the name of the job

#SBATCH --partition=GPU
#This sets the partition to the GPU partition. Important for GPU jobs

#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
#This allocates 1 GPU as a Global Resource (gres). Important for GPU jobs

#SBATCH --ntasks=10
#This sets the number of processes to 10.

#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#This allocates the number of cpus per tasks. 

#SBATCH --time=01:00:00 
#This allocates the walltime to 60 minutes. The program will not run for longer.

export GMX_IMGDIR=${SIFDIR}/gromacs/
export GMX_IMG=gromacs-2022.3_20230206.sif
export TOPOL_FILE=topol.tpr

singularity run --nv -B ${PWD}:/host_pwd --pwd /host_pwd  $GMX_IMGDIR/$GMX_IMG gmx mdrun -ntmpi 1 -nb gpu -pin on -v -noconfout -nsteps 5000 -ntomp ${SLURM_NTASKS} -s $TOPOL_FILE
#DO NOT USE 'srun' as it launches multiple independent jobs
